data.gender_notes: AlFatihah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name AlFatihah is derived from the first chapter of the Quran, Surah Al-Fatihah. This surah is recited during every rakah (unit) of prayer and is considered the 'opener' of the Quran. It invokes God's blessings and guidance. The name AlFatihah carries the meaning “The Opener” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose AlFatihah usually hope their child will grow to embody the opener and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of devotion and connection to God.

in_english.name: AlFatihah
in_english.meaning: The opening chapter of the Quran, containing the first six verses
in_english.long_meaning: AlFatihah is the opening chapter of the Quran, comprising the first six verses, which are considered the most recited and revered verses in the Quran. The word AlFatihah is derived from the Arabic root word Fat-ha, which means to open or reveal. The chapter AlFatihah is considered a prayer and a praise to Allah, and is recited in every prayer. It is also known as the 'Mother of the Quran' and is considered a source of guidance and wisdom. The chapter AlFatihah is composed of six verses, each of which contains a unique and profound message. The first verse, 'Alhamdu lillahi Rabb il-'alamin', is a declaration of praise and gratitude to Allah. The second verse, 'Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim', is a declaration of Allah's mercy and compassion. The third verse, 'Maliki yawmi d-din', is a declaration of Allah's sovereignty and authority. The fourth verse, 'Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'een', is a declaration of devotion and submission to Allah. The fifth verse, 'Ihdina siratal mustaqim', is a declaration of guidance and direction. The sixth verse, 'Siratal ladhiyyina an'amta 'alayhim', is a declaration of Allah's mercy and blessings. AlFatihah is considered a source of spiritual growth and development, and is recited by Muslims around the world to seek guidance and blessings.
